header.title: Concentration ratios by selected industry grouping
tablenote: The statistical table presents the Concentration Ratios (CR) in terms of business receipts, which are useful for analysing the extent of business concentration in selected industry groups of Hong Kong. It should be noted that analysis of CR should focus on temporal comparison rather than cross-industry comparison, because the size of individual industries may differ widely, and smaller-sized industries generally tend to have higher values of CR. For concepts, methods, definitions of terms and notes relating to the CR statistics, please refer to the feature article "Statistics on Sectoral Concentration".  The above-mentioned feature article is normally published every two years. It presents the CR statistics for more industry groups and broadly highlights some key observations.

CR(n) refers to the proportion of total business receipts which a given number of companies (n) from the top in the industry account for. The value of CR(n) lies between 0 and 1. For a given value of n, higher values of CR(n) indicate greater sectoral concentration.

Local representative offices of foreign banks are classified under the banking industry. However, as they have no business receipts, they are not included in the calculation of CR of the banking industry.
[+§4] CRn larger than or equal to 0.995
